topic: Country with the most camels: Somalia (FAO live-animal stocks, 7 million+), then Sudan and Kenya; Saudi Arabia under 2 million; Australia holds the largest feral (wild-living) herd, estimated at roughly 300,000.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Saudi Arabia has the most camels because camels mean Arabia.
myths.reality: FAO stock data put Somalia first with more than 7 million camels; Saudi Arabia keeps under 2 million.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Feed clips name Somalia as a one-liner; nobody builds the table against Arabia, wipes the assumption off the screen and then sets Australia's feral herd against it on a moving map.

fao_qcl.title: Crops and livestock products — live animals, camels, stocks
fao_qcl.notes: camel stocks by country: Somalia > 7 million (largest), Sudan ~4.9 million, Kenya ~3 million, Saudi Arabia ~1.5–1.8 million

worldmapper.title: Camels (2016)
worldmapper.notes: the world's largest camel population — more than 7 million — lives in Somalia, followed by Sudan and Kenya; first country outside Africa is Pakistan in 8th place

britannica_camel.title: Camel — mammal
britannica_camel.notes: dromedaries domesticated in Arabia; feral dromedary population in Australia; camels used for milk, meat, transport

dcceew_camels.title: Feral camels
dcceew_camels.notes: camels introduced to Australia in the 19th century; feral population in the arid interior, estimated at about 300,000 after the 2009–13 control programme; the largest wild dromedary herd in the world

fao_somalia.title: Somalia — livestock and camel milk
fao_somalia.notes: livestock is the backbone of the Somali economy; camel milk widely produced and sold; camels central to food, transport and wealth

wiki_somaliland.notes: self-declared republic since 1991, internationally unrecognised; claimed by Somalia

wiki_ilemi.title: Ilemi Triangle
wiki_ilemi.notes: administered by Kenya; claimed by South Sudan

claims.text: Somalia has the most camels of any country: more than 7 million, in a country of about 18 million people.
vo: which nation has the most camels
somalia. more than 7 million camels, the most of any nation, in a country of 18 million people

claims.text: Sudan has about 5 million camels, Kenya around 3 million; Saudi Arabia keeps under 2 million.
vo: sudan follows with about 5 million, kenya around 3. saudi arabia, the land of the camel, keeps under 2 million

claims.text: Camels are not native to Australia; about 300,000 feral dromedaries roam the arid interior — the largest wild herd anywhere.
vo: and australia? camels are not native there, yet about 300,000 feral ones roam the outback, more than anywhere

claims.text: In Somalia camels provide food, transport and wealth; camel milk is sold widely.
vo: in somalia the camel is food, transport and wealth; its milk is sold in every town
